title: Al-Fattah, the Opener
hookLine: the Opener, of doors, of hearts, of ways out

lines: A TREATY THAT FELT LIKE A LOSS.
cards: Remember Hudaybiyyah, eleven days ago, where the name ar-Rahman was struck from the treaty's first line? The rest of it felt worse. The Muslims had come to visit the Ka'ba and were sent home without reaching it.

Some of the terms looked one-sided. Many companions were deeply upset; Umar, Bukhari records, went to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ asking why they should accept such terms. They rode back toward Medina with their heads down.
On the way, a surah came down, and its first line called that treaty a clear victory. The Arabic word for victory there is the same word as opening.

teach.b: The first line of Surah al-Fath: We have opened for you a clear opening, a clear victory. The root is f-t-h, to open. It gives miftah, a key.
It gives fath, an opening, and a victory, because a victory is a way through. And it gives the name of the first surah you learned: al-Fatiha, the opening.

The treaty that looked like a door slamming turned out to be a door opening: two years of peace, in which, historians say, more people entered Islam than in all the years before. Al-Fattah is the one who opens.
In Surah Saba' the name has a second shade: our Lord will bring us together, then He will open between us with truth, and He is al-Fattah, al-'Alim, the Opener, the All-Knowing.
Here opening means judging: laying a dispute open so the truth is seen. In Surah Fatir, whatever mercy Allah opens for people, no one can hold back; whatever He holds back, no one can release.
In al-An'am: with Him are the keys of the unseen.
So the name covers every kind of stuck: a locked door, a locked-up heart, a dispute no one can settle, a way out you can't see.
Entering a mosque, many Muslims say words the Prophet taught, recorded by Muslim: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy. The one entering asks; the opening is left to al-Fattah.

how: Many Muslims say Allahumma iftah li abwaba rahmatik, O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy, when entering a mosque, and call on al-Fattah when a matter is stuck, asking for an opening.

o: the one who closes every door for good
the one who opens, and judges between people
the one who begins every new thing

games.q: the family of f-t-h — tap the pairs.

s: the Qur'an called the treaty of Hudaybiyyah a defeat
Surah al-Fath opens by calling it a clear victory, a clear opening.
al-Fatiha and al-Fattah share a root
in Surah Saba', opening also means judging between people
He opens between us with truth: He is al-Fattah, al-'Alim.

games.q: you're riding home from Hudaybiyyah, turned away from Mecca, upset by the terms. what does the surah revealed on the way say?
o: you have been defeated this time
We have opened for you a clear victory
games.why: 48:1: a clear opening, a clear victory. the peace that followed opened far more than it closed.

practice: Name one thing in your life that feels stuck, a conversation going nowhere, a job search, a friendship gone cold, something in you that won't budge, and picture it as a closed door.

Don't push on it; stand in front of it, breathe, and let not holding the key be a relief instead of a fear. If you pray, you can ask Allah, al-Fattah, to open it, or to open another way you haven't seen.

wordCard.voice: Al-Fattah. The Opener, of doors, hearts and ways out, and the one who opens the truth between people. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Opener, the Judge who lays truth open; from f-t-h, to open.

carryVoice: Your line: the opener. A treaty that felt like a loss was called a clear opening. Day two hundred forty-six is yours.

sources.ref: Qur'an 48:1 (a clear victory, a clear opening)
Qur'an 34:26 (He will open between us with truth; He is al-Fattah, al-'Alim)
Qur'an 35:2; 6:59 (mercy He opens none can withhold; the keys of the unseen)
Sahih Muslim 713 (open for me the doors of Your mercy)
